langues.write a comprehensive analysis on how s: In today'se world, social media platforms like Instagram have become a ubiquitinous presence in the lives of teenagers and young adults alike; they are not only spaces for self-expression but also arenas where body image concerns can be amplified due to their visual nature. The following essay will delve into how these digital platforms influence adolescents' perceptions about physical appearance, with a particular focus on the impact of Instagram and Facebook as primary sources of social comparison among teenagers aged 13-20 years old in South Africa (Kim et al., 2019). The essay will explore how these platforms contribute to body dissatisfaction through their portrayal of idealized images, the subsequent impact on self and identity development during adolescence. It is essential for health professionals working with this age group in South Africa (Kim et al., 2019) as well as parents/guardians who are concerned about body image issues to understand how social media platforms like Instagram can affect the mental, emotional and physical development of teenagers. This essay will discuss three main reasons why this is a critical issue: (i) The prevalence of these sites; (ii) Social comparison theory suggests that individuals compare themselves with others in order to evaluate their own self-worth or social standing within the group, which can lead them into negative body image and dissatisfaction. This essay will discuss how Instagram's role as a platform for sharing images has led many teenagers today (especially females) towards unhealthy dieting behaviors in an attempt to achieve their idealized bodies; this is further discussed by the study of Katz et al., 2019. The essay will also discuss how social media platforms like Instagram can be used as a tool for body positivity and health promotion, rather than just being seen solely through negative lenses (Kim & Lee-Newburn, 2018). This paper explores the impact of Facebook on adolescents' perceptions about their bodies. The study by Kim et al., which was conducted in South Korea with a sample size of over two thousand high school students aged between fifteen and eighteen years old (Kim & Lee-Newburn, 2018), found that the more time spent on Facebook or Instagram platforms like Snapchat, Twitter, TikTok etc., teenagers are exposed to unrealistic body images.
